Galium.



Galium aparine. Cleavers. Goose-grass. N. O. Galiaceæ (considered by some
        a sub-order of Rubiaceæ). Tincture and infusion of fresh plant. Extract. Poultices.



Clinical. ─   Bladder, irritability of. Calculus.   Cancer  . Gravel. Psoriasis. Ulcers.



Characteristics. ─     Galium
        has had no proving, but it is a popular remedy for cancer given internally and used
        externally; and also for scrofulous swellings and ulcers. It is further used as a diuretic
        and as a solvent for gravel and stone. It has cured a case of nodulated tumour of the tongue
        diagnosed to be cancer (  see   Hale); and a case of
        psoriasis of the hand (left) has been reported cured. Substantial doses were given in each
        case, and in the latter poultices of the herb were used as well.
